title: I'm going to run 100 trading bot backtests a day and share what I find.
author: According_Set990
selftext:
**I'm going to run 100 trading bot backtests a day and share what I find.**

I've spent a lot of time looking at EAs and automated trading strategies, and I keep running into the same problem:

There are thousands of bots out there, but it's incredibly difficult to separate something genuinely interesting from something that's simply been optimized to produce a beautiful backtest.

So I'm starting an experiment.

My goal is to run roughly **100 standardized backtests every day**, along with forward tests where possible, and document the results.

I'm not looking for a "holy grail" or a bot that prints money.

I'm looking for something much simpler:

**Can we systematically find bots that are worth investigating further for a potential edge?**

And just as importantly, I want to make the results useful for people who want to learn how to evaluate automated strategies themselves.

Things like:

• What does a healthy equity curve actually look like?  
• How much drawdown is too much?  
• When is a high win rate actually a warning sign?  
• How do you spot martingale/grid behavior?  
• How do you recognize overfitting?  
• What happens when you change the market, period, spread or parameters?  
• Does the strategy hold up out-of-sample?  
• Does it continue performing when forward tested?

Over time, I'm hoping this turns into a pretty large dataset.

Some tests will probably be terrible.

Most will probably be uninteresting.

But if we're testing hundreds and eventually thousands of strategies, the interesting question becomes:

**What survives the filtering process?**

I'll share the good, the bad and the ridiculous results rather than only posting the winners.

If there's interest here, I can post regular summaries of what I'm finding and break down some of the more interesting bots in detail.

**Also: give me EAs/bots you think I should test.**

Free, paid, popular, obscure, suspiciously good-looking;  doesn't matter.

Drop the name/link below and I'll start building a testing list.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: run a hundred a day and the best one each day will look great from luck alone, so the number worth publishing next to any winner is how many you ran to find it. a bot that only survives at one spread setting has already told you what it is.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 100 a day means by friday you've got 500 tries and a handful you'll want to share, which is the same beautiful-backtest filter you're trying to escape. post how many got tested next to each one you show and it stays honest.

comments.author: strat-run
comments.body:
You are are testing other people's bots then isn't the out of sample question impossible to answer? You can't trust that the bot wasn't tuned to overfit on your entire date range.

And over fitting is difficult to answer, you can grid sweep the bots parameters and make sure it's not an outlier from its neighbors.

You'd be better of collecting the bots, freezing them, and paper trading them for a year.
